absent: AUSENTE: Locking and concurrency rules for guarded stack allocation breakpoint management and floating state save beyond preemption control shown.
AUSENTE: Exact hardware register bit layouts and privileged control field positions.
AUSENTE: Full lifecycle and error handling for firmware reboot platform restart and secondary processor stop.
AUSENTE: Complete semantics for floating vector matrix memory tagging partitioning and authentication switching referenced but not routed.
AUSENTE: Scheduling affinity deadline and resource limit enforcement details beyond compatibility checks shown.
AUSENTE: Signal fault and exception delivery behavior for timestamp faults overlay faults and tag faults.

findings.text: Provides host lifecycle controls for idle termination shutdown halt poweroff and restart. Shutdown quiesces secondary processors targeting the designated reboot processor. Halt poweroff and restart first suppress local interrupts and request remote processors to stop. Restart prefers firmware runtime reset when that service is present then delegates to platform restart and otherwise remains halted with a diagnostic notice.

Exposes thread reset release and new execution setup. Flush clears floating thread local debug tagged address overlay and guarded stack state through dedicated helpers. Release discards floating state for the exiting task. New execution setup adjusts address space classification affinity and user facing controls as detailed separately.

Creates register context for a new thread with distinct handling for user clones versus kernel threads. User clones inherit parent registers with cleared return value and stack selected according to execution width plus thread local overlay and guarded stack inheritance. Kernel threads start from cleared registers with privileged status that forbids legitimate exception return and with entry routine arguments placed in preserved context. All paths converge on a common fork return address unwinder linkage and debug state reset.

Performs full context transfer between previous and next tasks covering floating thread local breakpoint identifier entry tracking speculative store bypass timer access authentication overlay and guarded stack switching followed by ordering barriers and late switching for memory tagging system control and partitioning. Ends with low level register context transfer returning the previous task. Debug validation of interrupt masking runs at entry.

Exposes user control entry points for tagged address retrieval and update timestamp counter access mode speculative bypass selection and compatibility execution checks. Tagged controls reject legacy width tasks. Timestamp mode and speculative controls translate abstract enable and disable requests into thread flags and hardware register updates. Compatibility check gates legacy binaries on platform support file type execution flag mask and affinity feasibility on mixed capability systems.

Provides guarded stack allocation and mode programming. Allocation reports empty success when the extension is unsupported or disabled for the task. Otherwise sharing address space triggers fresh stack creation sized from clone stack hints clamped between page granularity and resource limit derived bounds, while non sharing clones inherit the current pointer. Mode programming derives privileged control fields from user visible enable write and push requests.

Thread local state preserves current user pointer before installing next state. Preservation captures user pointer always and captures secondary user pointer only when supported and running in native width. Switching installs legacy read only pointer for compat width tasks and clears it otherwise, then installs primary and secondary pointers. Flush clears primary and secondary state and for compat width also clears shadow value with ordering enforced between shadow and hardware.

Duplication saves effective floating state from the source then copies the task image and sanitizes the destination to a non streaming baseline with no vector or matrix storage references and with related thread flags and control bits cleared including pending asynchronous fault state. Matrix extension storage is reallocated and enabled for the destination only when the source has it active, with cleanup of partial allocation on failure.

Guarded stack flush and copy have active and inert variants selected by feature availability. Active flush clears thread tracked base size pointer and mode plus lock state and restores restrictive privileged control. Active copy initializes base and size to empty inherits mode and lock state from the creator then attempts stack allocation and propagates allocation failures. Inert variants perform no action and report success. Switching preserves current pointer unconditionally then installs next pointer and refreshes mode on change with an additional barrier when either side has the feature enabled.

Permission overlay state is flushed to a fixed initial value at thread reset and preserved across duplication for user clones via hardware read while kernel threads start from the same initial value. Switching saves current hardware value into current thread storage and installs next value only when different, tolerating transient faults without extra synchronization.

User access to virtual counter is denied when the thread requests faulting behavior or when platform errata handling requires trapping, including an additional legacy width erratum case. Otherwise access is granted. Switch time refresh occurs only when the relevant width and faulting flags differ between previous and next threads.

Speculative store bypass switching takes no action for kernel threads and takes no action when the hardware capability is universally present since architectural state already transfers. Otherwise it applies per task mitigation state for the incoming task.

Flushing debug state iterates over breakpoint and watchpoint slots unregistering any installed hardware breakpoint and clearing the slot. Copying thread debug state for a new task simply clears the entire debug tracking structure so the child starts with no inherited hardware breakpoints.

New execution classifies address space as legacy width or native and adjusts allowed processor affinity on mixed capability systems to restrict legacy tasks to capable processors while relaxing restriction for native tasks. It then initializes authentication and tagging defaults reenables timestamp access and reenables speculation when the task had requested disable only until execution.

Legacy binary acceptance requires platform support for legacy user execution plus expected machine type and execution flag mask. On mixed capability systems it additionally requires that deadline constrained tasks retain admissible affinity against the legacy capable processor set.

Wait channel tracking pairs a resolved scheduler wait address with a bounded visit count used to terminate stack traversal. The callback records the initial address outside scheduler functions and otherwise continues while within a small bound.

Branch type reporting uses a compact table indexed by shifted branch type encoding to yield short human readable labels for absent jump call and combined cases. Entry tracking uses per processor storage for the current entry task updated on every switch. Tagged address availability is governed by a global disable flag consulted during enable requests.

Speculative bypass control accepts enable force disable disable and disable until execution requests. Enable clears noexec and disable markers and clears the mitigation thread flag. Disable and force disable set the disable marker and mitigation flag with force additionally latching a persistent disable marker. Disable until execution sets mitigation and latches a noexec marker that later execution clears by reenabling. Requests fail when global policy forces the opposite direction or when a persistent disable marker blocks reenabling. Unknown selectors are rejected and non bypass selectors report absence of device.

Timestamp mode toggles between faulting and enabled states. Invalid selectors are rejected. Valid updates atomically adjust the faulting thread flag and synchronize hardware access control under disabled preemption.

Tagged address control is unavailable to legacy width tasks for retrieval and update. Valid update mask always includes enable and when memory tagging is supported extends to synchronous asynchronous tag mask and optionally store only behavior. Updates reject unknown bits reject enable when globally disabled reject tagging configuration failures and otherwise install the enable flag. Retrieval reports enable state combined with current tagging configuration.

Guarded stack user mode is encoded from independent enable write and push requests into privileged control fields for checking selection store and push permissions atop a restrictive baseline. Switching reprograms control only when mode differs between threads.

Matrix extension and secondary thread pointer are treated as a pair across creation. Address space sharing creation clears secondary pointer and asserts matrix state is off. Non sharing creation inherits secondary pointer from hardware and duplicates matrix storage when source has it active. Duplication alone never inherits matrix state with inheritance occurring later during creation handling.

Timestamp flag updates are protected by disabling preemption across flag change and hardware synchronization. Compat thread local flush enforces ordering between shadow and hardware writes. Context switching issues a full inner shareable barrier before late memory tagging control and partitioning switches to make prior maintenance and page table effects visible and to satisfy cross processor ordering, with an additional guarded stack barrier when either thread uses guarded stacks.

Halt poweroff and failed restart never return and spin indefinitely after stopping other processors. Restart failure is announced before spinning. Switch entry validates expected interrupt mask and priority mask state and emits a warning on mismatch with distinct expectations depending on whether priority masking is in use.

Stack alignment applies address space randomization by subtracting a bounded random offset when enabled then aligns to required boundary. Wait channel lookup safely acquires task stack and walks with a bounded callback that skips scheduler addresses up to a small limit reporting failure when the stack cannot be acquired or no non scheduler address is found.

Branch type table covers NONE JC C and J encodings with corresponding short labels. Thread creation interprets CLONE_VM to detect address space sharing CLONE_SETTLS to detect explicit thread local assignment and CLONE_VFORK alongside sharing checks during guarded stack decisions. Presence of a start routine distinguishes kernel threads from user clones.

Tagged address and memory tagging controls use PR_TAGGED_ADDR_ENABLE plus PR_MTE_TCF_SYNC PR_MTE_TCF_ASYNC PR_MTE_TAG_MASK and optionally PR_MTE_STORE_ONLY when supported. Timestamp control uses PR_TSC_ENABLE and PR_TSC_SIGSEGV to select faulting behavior. Speculative bypass control uses PR_SPEC_STORE_BYPASS as selector with PR_SPEC_ENABLE PR_SPEC_DISABLE PR_SPEC_FORCE_DISABLE and PR_SPEC_DISABLE_NOEXEC as actions.

Guarded stack mode uses PR_SHADOW_STACK_ENABLE PR_SHADOW_STACK_WRITE and PR_SHADOW_STACK_PUSH to request checking store and push permissions. Timer access control uses ARCH_TIMER_USR_VCT_ACCESS_EN to gate user counter reads. Thread flag and capability checks involve TIF_TAGGED_ADDR TIF_TSC_SIGSEGV TIF_SSBD TIF_SME TIF_SVE and TIF_MTE_ASYNC_FAULT plus related spec markers and capabilities including ARM64_SSBS ARM64_MTE_STORE_ONLY and erratum related capabilities.
